posts.title: Devlog: CLS 2.0-dev1, the first release of the 2.0 series
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: First release of the 2.0 series: a complete rewrite in Rust with a JIT interpreter (CLS → WASM → wasmtime), static type checker, OOP, CMX and bindings. We compare against 1.1 and 1.2, and the first binaries are now available.

posts.title: Announcement: CLS 2.X, the path we're building
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: We're announcing the direction of the next generation of CLS: the 2.X series. Rewritten in Rust with static typing and a JIT interpreter, in development and wrapping up QA evaluations before the first stable release.

posts.title: Announcement: the current state of CLS 2.0-dev1
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: The 2.0-dev1 is now published. The latest JIT benchmark (fused WASM internals) puts it on par with C++/Rust in arithmetic and 100x+ faster than Python on several tests: fib ×330, arrays ×493 and calls ×480 over the baseline.

posts.title: Devlog: CLS 1.2, the Cython rewrite
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: The attempt to solve compile times by rewriting CLS from scratch in Cython, why the limited portability of native binaries ended the project, and the lesson that led to 2.0.

posts.title: Devlog: CLS 1.0-1.1, the version that consolidated the language
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: The first official and numbered version of CLS: its Python transpiler engine, the language with modules, classes and CMX, the experiments around it — and why it was not the first implementation of the language.

posts.title: Devlog: CLSJS, the JavaScript engine
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: The full port of the engine to JavaScript: the desline/parselex/estructuration/generator/jump pipeline, CLS running in the browser, the openserver and the first appearance of CMX.

posts.title: Devlog: the first CLS in Python (cls_py and cls_py2.2)
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: The jump from Batch to Python: the cls_py and cls_py2.2 implementations with their own lexer, the fub/include syntax, the stdlib with clv and impo, the pickle-based DLLs and the ancestor of everything that came next.

posts.title: Devlog: the origins, CLS in Batch
posts.author: CLS Team
posts.excerpt: The true origin of CLS: a fragile prototype written in cmd Batch in 2017, the many rewrites of the prototype era and why 1.0 was not the first implementation of the language.
